text:
maria: heads-up — starting a focused load test this morning targeting kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache behavior. goal: apples-to-apples perf comparison between kernel variants and autoscale behavior for dedicated pools. plan attached below.

aj: 👍 what's the harness? replay or synthetic?

maria: synthetic replay harness (replay traces + randomized prefixes). two modes: steady-state QPS and burst/scale tests. config excerpt: 
```
mode: replay
seed_traces: s3://redwood-test/traces/conv-1k.json
qps_targets: [50, 200, 800]
concurrency: 16
seq_len_dist: {short:0.6, medium:0.3, long:0.1}
kernel_variants: [fast-attn-opt, fallback-matmul, quant-ln]
batching: {max_tokens:2048, max_batch:64, wait_ms:5}
kv_warmup: [none, preload-10k, preload-50k]
```

maria: for autoscale tests we'll spin a dedicated pool (g4dn-like sim) and measure scale-up time, cold-start latency, and whether burst credits prevent immediate fallback to hosted tier.

liam: sgtm. can you also run the same suite with continuous-batching toggles? i'm curious about the p95 delta when batching waits 2ms vs 10ms.

maria: yes — will run wait_ms=2/5/10. also kernel selection logging enabled so we can attribute slow tails to kernel fallbacks.

kevin: FYI last week's perf-regression looked exactly like a kernel fallback on long sequences. p95 jumped ~120ms after the new matmul patch.

maria: yep. initial hypothesis: the scheduler started picking fallback-matmul for 16k kv-cache entries because the optimal kernels didn't have a plan for >8k kv sizes. testing will confirm.

janet: how are you measuring KV cache hit/miss impact? i.e., cold vs warmed cache?

maria: two dims: 1) cold start where kv cache empty, measure first-request latency and subsequent ramp; 2) warmed scenario where we preload prefixes (preload-10k/50k). also track memory pressure and evictions.

perf-bot: test-run queued (id: tr-2024-11-18-01). estimated duration: 45m.

deploy-bot: dedicated-pool spin-up started for pool id dp-09 (target 8 nodes).

aj: can we force kernel selection pins? i want an apples-to-apples run where only kernel differs.

maria: yes — will pin kernel and quantization profile per-run and use identical harness seeds. that's the apples-to-apples part.

liam: also include metrics for token-per-second and cost-est estimate per 1M tokens. helps tradeoffs when a faster kernel is more costly.

maria: noted. adding cost_est field.

--- 35 minutes later ---

perf-bot: tr-2024-11-18-01 completed. summary: steady-state 200 QPS run done. artifacts: s3://redwood-test/results/tr-2024-11-18-01/

maria: quick highlights from the first pass:
- fast-attn-opt: p50=34ms p95=78ms p99=132ms tps=7.1k tokens/s cost_est=$0.078 per 1k tokens
- fallback-matmul: p50=39ms p95=180ms p99=420ms tps=6.0k tokens/s cost_est=$0.065 per 1k tokens
- quant-ln: p50=36ms p95=95ms p99=150ms tps=7.0k tokens/s cost_est=$0.052 per 1k tokens
notes: the fallback variant has a much heavier p95/p99 tail due to frequent path through large-matmul kernel when long sequences hit. quant variant saves cost but slightly increases p50.

kevin: confirms earlier theory. fallback-matmul triggers for seq_len > ~3000 (KV entries > ~8k). we saw a kernel-change spike in the logs right before tail events.

liam: what about batching wait_ms variation?

maria: wait_ms=2ms gave lower p50 but increased CPU scheduling churn for tiny batches; p95 improved only for fast-attn-opt. wait_ms=10ms increased throughput (tps +12%) but p95 for fallback-matmul got worse (more long sequences combined into big GEMMs).

janet: what about KV warmup?

maria: preload-50k reduced p99 by ~45% for all kernels. cold start first-request latency anchored at ~420ms for fallback case, warm runs had first-request ~120ms.

perf-bot: autoscale/burst test results: scale-up 1->4 nodes: median 38s, 90th 72s. cold-start tail (first 10 reqs after node add): median 290ms, p95 900ms. burst credits prevented fallback to hosted for bursts <= 3x baseline for up to 90s.

maria: takeaways so far:
- kernel selection mismatch is main driver of p95 regressions on long-KV workloads. need kernel-plan coverage for larger KV sizes or explicit kernel pinning fallback thresholds.
- batching wait tuning gives tradeoff between throughput and p95; suggest adaptive wait_ms based on observed seq_len dist.
- KV preload is a very effective mitigation for cold tails — consider automated prefix-warming for dedicated pools on scale-up.
- scale-up time is ~40s median; for tight latency SLOs we should pre-warm additional nodes or keep >0 burst capacity.

kevin: action items?

maria: short list: 
1) eng-runtime: add kernel plan for KV>8k (kevin + liam) — owner: kevin — due EOD next Thurs
2) perf: add adaptive wait_ms PoC in the batching scheduler (maria + aj) — due next Tue
3) infra: implement optional KV prefix-warm on node join (janet + infra) — due next Wed
4) product: review SLO doc re: cold-start allowances for dedicated pools (sre + product) — owner: liam — due next Fri

aj: i'll document the harness + commands for replay so QE can reproduce.

maria: thanks — I'll upload full logs and flamegraphs. attaching sample flamegraph path: s3://redwood-test/results/tr-2024-11-18-01/flamegraphs/fast-attn-opt.svg

sre-bot: created incident stub for "kv-plan-coverage" tracking ticket: RD-INF-8392

kevin: digging into kernel planner now. preliminary note: heuristics threshold was conservative to avoid register spills; might relax for large kv sizes with revised tiling.

maria: perfect. i'll post a shorter summary in #eng-announce after we have the kernel patch PR. thanks all. :rocket:
